items.title: Devlin nets first international goal as Northern Ireland beat Ukraine
items.excerpt: Terry Devlin's first international goal kept Northern Ireland top of their Nations League group as a 1-0 win over Ukraine set up a promotion decider away to Hungary on Tuesday.
body: Terry Devlin's first international goal kept Northern Ireland top of their Nations League group as a 1-0 win over Ukraine set up a promotion decider away to Hungary on Tuesday.

The 23-year-old Devlin has been in the goals for Portsmouth this term with four, and opened his Northern Ireland account with a fine strike in the 68th minute as he left Ukraine goalkeeper Anatoliy Trubin flat-footed with a shot from distance. Pierce Charles then made a superb save to deny Danylo Sikan at the death and preserve Northern Ireland's fifth straight clean sheet - the first time they have achieved that since 2017 - and ensure they remain the only side in the competition yet to concede.

items.title: Tuchel unhappy as anti-racism protocol questions overshadow Spain clash
items.excerpt: Thomas Tuchel insisted his words had been "twisted" as questions over anti-racism protocols overshadowed the build-up to England's Nations League showdown in Madrid.
body: Thomas Tuchel insisted his words had been "twisted" as questions over anti-racism protocols overshadowed the build-up to England's Nations League showdown in Madrid.
Tuchel was asked after England's win over Croatia on Thursday how he and England would react if racist abuse occurred during Sunday's game against Spain.
The head coach responded by saying he would "maybe take five minutes" to remind his players of the anti-racism protocols. Tuchel also said "we will not expect" any abuse to occur in Madrid.

items.title: Trafford to start in Spain - but what are Tuchel's other selection issues?
items.excerpt: Against the best team in the world, Thomas Tuchel's defensive decisions will be key. And he has many to make.
body: Against the best team in the world, Thomas Tuchel's defensive decisions will be key. And he has many to make.

The England head coach said before Croatia at Wembley on Thursday that he was quite happy to go full-strength in both matches, despite the three-day gap, and he was true to his word. All the big guns were out for Harry Kane's big night.

Barring unexpected late injury or illness, the best player in the world will lead the line against the world champions. Morgan Rogers should start at right wing, Anthony Gordon left wing. England's Madrid maestro Jude Bellingham will play No 10, and Elliot Anderson and Declan Rice will form the double pivot.
